criteria.description: Correctness of minimal path logic: on the docstring examples the code returns [1,2,1] for grid [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]], k=3 and [1] for k=1; in general it locates the cell with value 1, finds the smallest value among its edge-neighbors, and for k>1 returns length-k list alternating 1 and that minimal neighbor (starting with 1).

Boundary handling and termination: for all inputs in stated domain (N>=2, k>=1) the code terminates without crash or infinite loop, returns list of length k, correctly handles 1 positioned at corner/edge (2-3 neighbors) and both even and odd k.

Implementation validity and readability: returned body is syntactically valid Python, first line indentation fits inside function, no repeated def/docstring/Markdown, uses clear straightforward logic and returns list of ints.
